opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer. Engineers own Source Code, so admin is permitted per policy for full-time employees whose role owns the system. Requested admin is at the maximum level; recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin is above the maximum of read, so recommend granting read.
reason: Miguel Benson (E006) requested admin to Source Code. HR's note confirms he is a full-time Engineer (role and employment type looked up in HR's own database). Since Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, the policy permits admin for a full-time employee whose role owns the system, making the maximum level admin. The requested level (admin) equals the maximum, so admin is granted. (The Security note's contractor listing conflicts on employment type, but HR is authoritative for employment status, and the role Engineer is consistent across both notes.)
